Whenever something news worthy happens I tend to just search a few keywords in DuckDuckGo (don't use Google, ever) and read the articles that come up. I do however get tired of having to go through several pages of CNN, NBC, NYT propaganda etc before finding something believable so here is a short guide to filter the junk.

Mozilla Firefox:

  1. Pick an alternative default search engine if using Google:

    • DuckDuckGo (add-on to set as default search engine). I personally use DuckDuckGo as it comes with it's own uncensored search results but you can find equally viable alternatives here.
    • StartPage, if you want the exact Google search results without the tracking and data collection then pick this one.

  2. Install GreaseMonkey, this is an add-on which "Allows you to customize the way a web page displays or behaves, by using small bits of JavaScript. "

Continue with step 3.

Google Chrome: (Consider using SRWare Iron, same thing without your privacy being raped and all Google Chrome extensions work as well.)

  1. Pick an alternative default search engine if using Google:

    • DuckDuckGo (extension to set as default search engine). I personally use DuckDuckGo as it comes with it's own uncensored search results but you can find equally viable alternatives here.
    • StartPage, if you want the exact Google search results without the tracking and data collection then pick this one.

  2. Install TamperMonkey, this is an extension which basically the chrome version of GreaseMonkey.

Continue with step 3.

       3. Install Google Hit Hider by Domain (Search Filter / Block Sites), this is the script which will block and filter specific domains from your search results. Will work for both DuckDuckGo and StartPage, and yes for Google as well but again don't use Google. Optional 1 minute tutorial on how to use this.

       4. Now search "news" on DuckDuckGo and you will see a block button next to every search result. Click on it and choose either "Block site", if you want to hide that result with a small notice, or "Perma-ban", if you want to hide the result and never get a notice.

       5. Done and now enjoy your clean search results.

Let me know if you have any questions or suggestions, cheers!
